When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

content.content:
1	![model-router](assets/banner.png)
2	
3	# model-router
4	
5	Run Claude Code on every subscription you already pay for.
6	
7	Your main Claude session stays exactly as it is. This resource adds a local
8	"switchboard" (a proxy) that holds your OTHER subscription logins - ChatGPT,
9	Gemini, Grok, Kimi - and lets Claude Code send work to those models three
10	ways: as headless build workers, as whole terminal or VSCode sessions, or as
11	subagents. No API keys, no per-token bills - just the subscriptions you
12	already have. Every default (model, effort, turn cap) is changeable.
13	
14	## FabSol - the flow that combines them
15	
16	**FabSol lives in its own folder: [`skills/fabsol/`](skills/fabsol/SKILL.md).**
17	It is the flagship of this resource: the flow that orchestrates the two models
18	together. Your main model (Fable) plans, writes one self-contained spec per
19	task, and verifies - the routed worker model (Sol by default) does 100% of the
20	building. In our 7-test benchmark this shipped identical builds for 33% less
21	than the main model working alone, with most of the burn moved onto the second
22	subscription's spare capacity.
23	
24	Invoke it as `/model-router:fabsol <brief>` (plugin install) or `/fabsol <brief>`
25	(manual install). Everything else in this resource exists to support that flow.
26	
27	## Play it safe (read this first)
28	
29	Anthropic's terms (updated Feb 2026) ban using a Claude **subscription** login
30	inside third-party tools - so this resource NEVER routes your Claude login
31	through the proxy. The design is one-directional: Claude Code runs on its
32	normal direct login and REACHES OUT to the other models. Keep it that way.
33	
34	## What's inside
35	
36	| Folder | What it is |
37	|---|---|
38	| `skills/fabsol/` | **the FabSol flow** - orchestrator + worker (the flagship) |
39	| `skills/model-router/` | the routing knowledge - three usage modes, model switching |
40	| `commands/fabsol.md` | thin command that invokes the fabsol skill with your brief |
41	| `agents/worker.md` | build-worker subagent for routed sessions |
42	| `scripts/` | start-proxy, worker, session, vscode - each as `.sh` (Mac/Linux) and `.ps1` (Windows) |
43	| `proxy/config.example.yaml` | ready-to-copy proxy config |
44	
45	## Install - steps for the agent setting this up
46	
47	Work through these in order. Ask the user for their preference where a step
48	offers a choice.
49	
50	**Step 1 - install the proxy.** Download the latest
51	[CLIProxyAPI](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/releases) release
52	for the user's OS and unzip it somewhere stable (suggest `~/cli-proxy-api`).
53	
54	**Step 2 - configure it.** Copy this resource's `proxy/config.example.yaml`
55	to `config.yaml` next to the proxy binary. Have the user pick their own value
56	for the `api-keys` entry (any string - it is the local password between
57	Claude Code and the proxy; `my-proxy-key` is the placeholder this README
58	assumes).
59	
60	**Step 3 - log in to the other subscription(s).** Run from the proxy folder;
61	each opens a browser once and stores the login locally in `~/.cli-proxy-api`:
62	
63	```bash
64	./cli-proxy-api -config config.yaml -codex-login        # ChatGPT / Codex (default worker)
65	# also available, same pattern:
66	#   -antigravity-login   Google Antigravity / Gemini
67	#   -xai-login           xAI Grok
68	#   -kimi-login          Kimi
69	```
70	
71	**Step 4 - set the four env vars** in the user's shell profile (these are the
72	shipped defaults - see "Change the defaults" below):
73	
74	```bash
75	# Mac/Linux (~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc)
76	export MODEL_ROUTER_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8317"
77	export MODEL_ROUTER_KEY="my-proxy-key"        # the key from step 2
78	export MODEL_ROUTER_MODEL="gpt-5.6-sol"       # default worker model
79	export MODEL_ROUTER_EFFORT="low"              # default worker effort
80	```
81	
82	```powershell
83	# Windows (persist once, from PowerShell)
84	[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("MODEL_ROUTER_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8317", "User")
85	[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("MODEL_ROUTER_KEY", "my-proxy-key", "User")
86	[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("MODEL_ROUTER_MODEL", "gpt-5.6-sol", "User")
87	[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("MODEL_ROUTER_EFFORT", "low", "User")
88	```
89	
90	**Step 5 - install the pieces into Claude Code.** Two options, either works:
91	
92	- *Plugin route:* run `/plugin marketplace add <path-to-this-unzipped-folder>`
93	  then `/plugin install model-router@robonuggets`. Commands are namespaced:
94	  `/model-router:fabsol`.
95	- *Manual route:* copy `skills/fabsol/` and `skills/model-router/` into
96	  `~/.claude/skills/`, `commands/fabsol.md` into `~/.claude/commands/`

![model-router](assets/banner.png)

# model-router

Run Claude Code on every subscription you already pay for.

Your main Claude session stays exactly as it is. This resource adds a local
"switchboard" (a proxy) that holds your OTHER subscription logins - ChatGPT,
Gemini, Grok, Kimi - and lets Claude Code send work to those models three
ways: as headless build workers, as whole terminal or VSCode sessions, or as
subagents. No API keys, no per-token bills - just the subscriptions you
already have. Every default (model, effort, turn cap) is changeable.

## FabSol - the flow that combines them

**FabSol lives in its own folder: [`skills/fabsol/`](skills/fabsol/SKILL.md).**
It is the flagship of this resource: the flow that orchestrates the two models
together. Your main model (Fable) plans, writes one self-contained spec per
task, and verifies - the routed worker model (Sol by default) does 100% of the
building. In our 7-test benchmark this shipped identical builds for 33% less
than the main model working alone, with most of the burn moved onto the second
subscription's spare capacity.

Invoke it as `/model-router:fabsol <brief>` (plugin install) or `/fabsol <brief>`
(manual install). Everything else in this resource exists to support that flow.

## Play it safe (read this first)

Anthropic's terms (updated Feb 2026) ban using a Claude **subscription** login
inside third-party tools - so this resource NEVER routes your Claude login
through the proxy. The design is one-directional: Claude Code runs on its
normal direct login and REACHES OUT to the other models. Keep it that way.

## What's inside

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `skills/fabsol/` | **the FabSol flow** - orchestrator + worker (the flagship) |
| `skills/model-router/` | the routing knowledge - three usage modes, model switching |
| `commands/fabsol.md` | thin command that invokes the fabsol skill with your brief |
| `agents/worker.md` | build-worker subagent for routed sessions |
| `scripts/` | start-proxy, worker, session, vscode - each as `.sh` (Mac/Linux) and `.ps1` (Windows) |
| `proxy/config.example.yaml` | ready-to-copy proxy config |

## Install - steps for the agent setting this up

Work through these in order. Ask the user for their preference where a step
offers a choice.

**Step 1 - install the proxy.** Download the latest
[CLIProxyAPI](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/releases) release
for the user's OS and unzip it somewhere stable (suggest `~/cli-proxy-api`).

**Step 2 - configure it.** Copy this resource's `proxy/config.example.yaml`
to `config.yaml` next to the proxy binary. Have the user pick their own value
for the `api-keys` entry (any string - it is the local password between
Claude Code and the proxy; `my-proxy-key` is the placeholder this README
assumes).

**Step 3 - log in to the other subscription(s).** Run from the proxy folder;
each opens a browser once and stores the login locally in `~/.cli-proxy-api`:

```bash
./cli-proxy-api -config config.yaml -codex-login        # ChatGPT / Codex (default worker)
# also available, same pattern:
#   -antigravity-login   Google Antigravity / Gemini
#   -xai-login           xAI Grok
#   -kimi-login          Kimi
```

**Step 4 - set the four env vars** in the user's shell profile (these are the
shipped defaults - see "Change the defaults" below):

```bash
# Mac/Linux (~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc)
export MODEL_ROUTER_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8317"
export MODEL_ROUTER_KEY="my-proxy-key"        # the key from step 2
export MODEL_ROUTER_MODEL="gpt-5.6-sol"       # default worker model
export MODEL_ROUTER_EFFORT="low"              # default worker effort
```

```powershell
# Windows (persist once, from PowerShell)
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("MODEL_ROUTER_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8317", "User")
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("MODEL_ROUTER_KEY", "my-proxy-key", "User")
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("MODEL_ROUTER_MODEL", "gpt-5.6-sol", "User")
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("MODEL_ROUTER_EFFORT", "low", "User")
```

**Step 5 - install the pieces into Claude Code.** Two options, either works:

- *Plugin route:* run `/plugin marketplace add <path-to-this-unzipped-folder>`
  then `/plugin install model-router@robonuggets`. Commands are namespaced:
  `/model-router:fabsol`.
- *Manual route:* copy `skills/fabsol/` and `skills/model-router/` into
  `~/.claude/skills/`, `commands/fabsol.md` into `~/.claude/commands/`
  (gives plain `/fabsol`), and `agents/worker.md` into `~/.claude/agents/`.

**Step 6 - verify.** Start the proxy (`scripts/start-proxy.sh` or `.ps1`),
then confirm the worker model is served:

```bash
curl -s "$MODEL_ROUTER_URL/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODEL_ROUTER_KEY"
```

Then run one cheap end-to-end test:

```bash
scripts/worker.sh "Reply with exactly: routing works"    # Windows: scripts\worker.ps1 "..."
```

If both answer, the setup is live. Try `/fabsol build me a small test page`.

## Change the defaults (everything is adjustable)

The resource SHIPS with: worker = `gpt-5.6-sol`, effort = `low`,
turn cap = `20`. Change any of them:

| What | How |
|---|---|
| Worker model, everywhere at once | set `MODEL_ROUTER_MODEL` to any ID your proxy serves |
| Worker model, one call | pass it as an argument (`scripts/worker.sh "task" gemini-3.5-flash`) or name it in your /fabsol brief |
| Worker effort | set `MODEL_ROUTER_EFFORT` (`low` ships; raise to `medium` if builds miss acceptance criteria - higher mostly burns tokens: in our tests xhigh made the worker grind 2-3x more turns for the same output) |
| Turn cap | edit `--max-turns 20` in `skills/fabsol/SKILL.md` (raise for bigger multi-file tasks) |
| Proxy address / key | `MODEL_ROUTER_URL` / `MODEL_ROUTER_KEY` |

**Which models can you point at?** Any ID your proxy serves. Discover them:

```bash
curl -s "$MODEL_ROUTER_URL/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODEL_ROUTER_KEY"
```

| Provider | Login flag | Example models |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI / Codex | `-codex-login` | `gpt-5.6-sol` (default), GPT-5.5 family |
| Google Antigravity / Gemini | `-antigravity-login` | Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, newer tiers where served |
| xAI Grok | `-xai-login` | Grok 4.5, Grok Composer 2.5 Fast |
| Kimi | `-kimi-login` | Kimi K2.7 Code, K2.6 |
| Google Vertex | `-vertex-import key.json` | your Vertex-served models |

Only providers you've logged into appear. Model IDs vary by CLIProxyAPI
version - always trust your own `/v1/models` list over this table.

## Launch Claude Code ON the routed model

Besides FabSol (where your normal session delegates), you can run a whole
Claude Code session on the routed model:

**Terminal:**

```bash
scripts/session.sh              # default worker model
scripts/session.sh grok-4.5     # any model your proxy serves
```

Windows: `scripts\session.ps1 [model]`. Or by hand - set the two env vars and
launch (scoped to that terminal, closes with it):

```powershell
$env:ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8317"
$env:ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "my-proxy-key"
claude --model gpt-5.6-sol
```

**VSCode:**

```bash
scripts/vscode.sh [folder]      # Windows: scripts\vscode.ps1 [folder]
```

Opens a VSCode window whose Claude Code sessions run on the routed model. It
uses a separate VSCode profile folder on purpose: an already-running VSCode
ignores env vars from new launches, so this is the way that always works.
Alternative if you prefer your normal profile: fully close VSCode, set the two
env vars in a terminal, then run `code .` from that terminal.

In a routed session (terminal or VSCode), the plugin's `worker` subagent
resolves too - so even subagents run on routed models there.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Connection refused" on delegation** - the proxy isn't running. Run the
  start-proxy script.
- **Auth error from the proxy** - your provider login expired. Re-run the login
  flag for that provider (step 3).
- **"Unknown provider for model X"** - that provider isn't logged in, or the ID
  is wrong. Check the `/v1/models` list.
- **VSCode window doesn't route** - VSCode was already running with its normal
  env. Use `scripts/vscode` (separate profile), or close VSCode fully first.
- **Worker output is weak** - the spec is doing too little work. The
  orchestrator must make every creative/architectural call in the spec; the
  worker just types. Raising `MODEL_ROUTER_EFFORT` to `medium` is the second lever.

## License

CC BY 4.0 - free to use, adapt, and share with attribution to RoboNuggets.

# Batch model routing

Apply this policy automatically when the user asks to ingest, continue, or process a Zotero library batch. The
bridge remains model-agnostic; routing belongs to the harness that orchestrates CLI and MCP calls.

## Default roles

| Stage | Codex model | Reasoning | Allowed work |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operations | `gpt-5.6-terra` | `high` | Backlog inspection, batch creation, extraction, metadata audit, Reference Stubs, reconciliation, integrity checks, tests, lint, and documentation |
| Scientific review | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `high` | Full-text methods/results/limitations review, applicability judgment, evidence-locator selection, Paper Brief writing, and final scientific approval |

Use `gpt-5.6-luna` only when the harness exposes it as an ephemeral worker and the task is strictly deterministic,
read-only status or hash validation. Otherwise use Terra. Never use Luna for Reference Stub relevance wording,
Paper Brief review, synthesis, or promotion.

## Automatic orchestration

1. Do not ask the user to choose a model for each stage unless they explicitly override this policy.
2. If the current task runs on Sol, keep Sol as the orchestrator/reviewer and send the operational stage to one
   Terra worker.
3. If the current task runs on Terra, keep Terra for operations and send each substantive full-text review stage
   to a Sol worker.
4. Use ephemeral subagents or workers, not separate user-owned threads, solely for model routing.
5. Run model-routed stages sequentially. Never allow two workers to write the same batch ledger, Promotion Record,
   or SecondBrain artifact concurrently.
6. Give each worker explicit ownership, the frozen batch ID and item keys, allowed write surfaces, stopping
   conditions, and required verification output.
7. Terra may save a Reference Stub only after the bridge confirms that Usable Full Text is unavailable. Terra must
   not save a Paper Brief.
8. Sol must inspect page-aware evidence and satisfy the Paper Brief contract before calling `save_paper_brief`.
9. Return control to Terra for reconciliation and deterministic verification after Sol finishes promotion.
10. Report the effective model route in the final checkpoint. If the harness cannot select worker models, complete
    the batch with the current model and state that no model switch occurred.

## Quality boundary

- Do not lower the evidence, applicability, locator, or limitation standards to save model cost.
- Escalate ambiguous citations, conflicting metadata, unclear methods, unsupported claims, or difficult
  applicability judgments to Sol even if they first appear during an operational stage.
- Use `xhigh` only for a specific difficult review that fails at `high`; do not make it the batch default.
- Preserve the user's explicit model choice when they name one for a particular task.

For non-Codex harnesses, map the same roles to that harness's balanced worker tier and flagship reasoning tier only
when explicit model routing is available. Never invent provider model IDs or claim that a switch occurred when the
harness cannot verify it.

It is in **both** `config.yaml` and `MODEL_ROUTER_KEY`. They must always match.

## What is left for you

**A. Log in to one other subscription.** Pick one and paste it into the prompt:

```
! cd ~/cli-proxy-api && ./cli-proxy-api -config config.yaml -codex-login
```

Other options, same pattern: `-antigravity-login` (Gemini), `-xai-login` (Grok),
`-kimi-login` (Kimi).

**B. Install the plugin.** Type these two lines in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add ~/.claude/vendor/model-router
/plugin install model-router@robonuggets
```

**C. Verify.** Start the proxy, then check the model list:

```
~/.claude/vendor/model-router/scripts/start-proxy.sh
curl -s "$MODEL_ROUTER_URL/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODEL_ROUTER_KEY"
```

If `gpt-5.6-sol` is not in that list, change `MODEL_ROUTER_MODEL` in `~/.zshrc`
to an ID that is. The README's model table is a guess; your own list is the truth.

## Safety rule (do not break this)

Only the four `MODEL_ROUTER_*` vars go in `~/.zshrc`.
Never put `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` there.
Those two are set per-command by the scripts. That keeps your own Claude login
off the proxy, which is what Anthropic's terms require.

---

# How this best applies to your setup

## 1. Best fit by far: `sports-science-research-grounding`

That skill already has a routing plan it cannot run.
`references/batch-model-routing.md` names `gpt-5.6-terra` for operations and
`gpt-5.6-sol` for scientific review. Rule 10 says: if the harness cannot pick
worker models, just finish on the current model and say no switch happened.

Right now that is always the outcome. Claude Code has no way to reach those models.

Model Router is exactly the missing piece. Once the Codex login is in, the
Terra/Sol split becomes real work instead of a written intention.

**Do this:** after login, add one line to `batch-model-routing.md` saying workers
run through `scripts/worker.sh "<spec>" gpt-5.6-terra high`. That is the whole hookup.

## 2. Also good: mechanical, high-volume build work

These burn a lot of tokens and need zero judgment once the spec is written.
That is the exact profile the routed worker is good at.

- `cli-printing-press` — generating a Go CLI from an OpenAPI spec. Long, repetitive,
  fully specified up front.
- `graphify` — bulk extraction across a folder of files.
- `five-slides-generator` — pptxgenjs code against a fixed template.

## 3. Keep these on your own model

Anything that judges your data or writes your memory:
`interview-me`, `weekly-review`, `status-report`, `improve-system`, `closeout`,
`memory-write`, `advisor`.

Two reasons. The output is only as good as the judgment behind it, and these
touch your SecondBrain and memory files. A cheaper worker saves little and risks
a bad write.

## 4. The one rule that decides everything

Ask: **can I write a spec that leaves the worker nothing to decide?**

Yes → route it. No → keep it.

The README says the same thing in its troubleshooting: weak worker output means
the spec did too little work, not that the model was too small.

## Realistic payoff

The claim is ~33% cheaper on build tasks. For you the bigger win is different:
your research-grounding batches move off your Claude quota entirely and onto
ChatGPT capacity you already pay for. Those batches are the long-running,
token-heavy ones. That is where the money is.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start CLIProxyAPI in the background if it is not already listening.
# Set CLIPROXY_DIR to where you installed cli-proxy-api (default: ~/cli-proxy-api).
DIR="${CLIPROXY_DIR:-$HOME/cli-proxy-api}"
URL="${MODEL_ROUTER_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8317}"
KEY="${MODEL_ROUTER_KEY:-my-proxy-key}"

if curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 2 "$URL/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"; then

# Model Router — setup notes (2026-08-15)

## Correction

An earlier draft of this file said Claude Code had no way to reach the Codex
models, so Model Router was the missing piece. **That was wrong.** Testing on this
machine proved you already have a direct path. The recommendation below is the
corrected one.

## What is installed

| Step | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Proxy installed | done | `~/cli-proxy-api/cli-proxy-api` (CLIProxyAPI v7.2.132, darwin arm64) |
| 2. Config written | done | `~/cli-proxy-api/config.yaml` |
| 3. Log in to a subscription | not done — and probably not needed, see below | |
| 4. Env vars set | done | `~/.zshrc`, block marked `# --- model-router ---` |
| 5. Resource staged | done | `~/.claude/vendor/model-router/` |
| 6. Verify | proxy starts, key works; model list empty until a login exists | |

Local proxy password: `mr-5ad27006368c75f1e98bca6c` (matches in `config.yaml`
and `MODEL_ROUTER_KEY`).

All of this is **inert** until a provider login exists. Nothing needs undoing.

## Safety rule

Only the four `MODEL_ROUTER_*` vars go in `~/.zshrc`.
Never `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`.
The proxy binary offers `-claude-login`. Do not use it — that is the one thing
Anthropic's terms forbid.

---

# What is actually true about your Codex setup

## You already have a direct line to Codex

Tested today, all working, no new software:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `codex exec "..."` | works — `gpt-5.6-sol`, high effort |
| `codex exec --model gpt-5.6-terra "..."` | works |
| `codex exec --model gpt-5.6-luna "..."` | works |

Codex CLI 0.147.0 at `/opt/homebrew/bin/codex`. Logged in on your ChatGPT
subscription (OAuth tokens, not an API key). Default already set to
`gpt-5.6-sol` at `high` in `~/.codex/config.toml`.

There is **no in-between model** on this path.

## The Sonnet thing you noticed — found it

`~/.claude/plugins/cache/openai-codex/codex/1.0.6/agents/codex-rescue.md`

Line 4 of its frontmatter: `model: sonnet`

That is the `codex:rescue` subagent. Its own instructions call it "a thin
forwarding wrapper" whose only job is to hand the task to Codex. It does no
thinking. But it is still a language model deciding whether to forward — and
sometimes it decides not to. That is why it felt like it wasn't hitting Codex.

**Fix: don't use the wrapper when you want Codex.** Call it straight:

```
codex exec --model gpt-5.6-sol "your task here"
```

Do **not** edit that agent file. It lives in a plugin cache and the next update
overwrites it. Editing it also would not remove the discretion problem.

---

# Corrected recommendation

## 1. For "go right to Codex" — use `codex exec`, not the proxy

Model-router gives you Claude Code *running on* a GPT model through a proxy.
`codex exec` gives you actual Codex. For your case the second is better: it is
already working, already authenticated, and has no middle layer.

## 2. `sports-science-research-grounding` is executable today

Its `references/batch-model-routing.md` assigns `gpt-5.6-terra` to operations and
`gpt-5.6-sol` to scientific review, then says to give up if the harness can't
switch models. It has been giving up unnecessarily. Both models answer right now.

**The change:** in that reference file, replace the "cannot select worker models"
escape hatch with the real command:

```
codex exec --model gpt-5.6-terra "<operations spec>"
codex exec --model gpt-5.6-sol   "<review spec>"
```

That is a small edit to one file and it turns a dormant policy into working
behavior. This is the highest-value thing on this page.

## 3. What Model Router is still worth keeping for

Two things `codex exec` cannot do:

- **`/fabsol`** — the orchestrate-and-verify flow where your main model writes
  the spec and the worker builds. Useful for `cli-printing-press`, `graphify`,
  `five-slides-generator` — mechanical, spec-driven, high token burn.
- **Non-OpenAI models** — Gemini, Grok, Kimi. Only worth a login if you actually
  hold one of those subscriptions.

If neither appeals, leave the proxy installed and unused. It costs nothing.

## 4. Do not log in to Codex on the proxy

It buys you nothing you don't already have, and it spends the same ChatGPT quota
through a longer path. Only log in to the proxy for a provider you can't already
reach.

## 5. Keep on your own model

`interview-me`, `weekly-review`, `status-report`, `improve-system`, `closeout`,
`memory-write`. These judge your data and write your memory.

## 6. The rule

**Can you write a spec that leaves the worker nothing to decide?**
Yes → route it. No → keep it.

---

## Unrelated thing worth knowing

Every `codex exec` run printed:

> Exceeded skills context budget. All skill descriptions were removed and 187
> additional skills were not included in the model-visible skills list.

Codex currently cannot see any of your skills. Separate problem, not caused by
anything here, but it means Codex is running blind to your tooling.

# Batch model routing

Apply this policy automatically when the user asks to ingest, continue, or process a Zotero library batch. The
bridge remains model-agnostic; routing belongs to the harness that orchestrates CLI and MCP calls.

## Default roles

| Stage | Codex model | Reasoning | Allowed work |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operations | `gpt-5.6-terra` | `high` | Backlog inspection, batch creation, extraction, metadata audit, Reference Stubs, reconciliation, integrity checks, tests, lint, and documentation |
| Scientific review | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `high` | Full-text methods/results/limitations review, applicability judgment, evidence-locator selection, Paper Brief writing, and final scientific approval |

Use `gpt-5.6-luna` only when the harness exposes it as an ephemeral worker and the task is strictly deterministic,
read-only status or hash validation. Otherwise use Terra. Never use Luna for Reference Stub relevance wording,
Paper Brief review, synthesis, or promotion.

## Automatic orchestration

1. Do not ask the user to choose a model for each stage unless they explicitly override this policy.
2. If the current task runs on Sol, keep Sol as the orchestrator/reviewer and send the operational stage to one
   Terra worker.
3. If the current task runs on Terra, keep Terra for operations and send each substantive full-text review stage
   to a Sol worker.
4. Use ephemeral subagents or workers, not separate user-owned threads, solely for model routing.
5. Run model-routed stages sequentially. Never allow two workers to write the same batch ledger, Promotion Record,
   or SecondBrain artifact concurrently.
6. Give each worker explicit ownership, the frozen batch ID and item keys, allowed write surfaces, stopping
   conditions, and required verification output.
7. Terra may save a Reference Stub only after the bridge confirms that Usable Full Text is unavailable. Terra must
   not save a Paper Brief.
8. Sol must inspect page-aware evidence and satisfy the Paper Brief contract before calling `save_paper_brief`.
9. Return control to Terra for reconciliation and deterministic verification after Sol finishes promotion.
10. Report the effective model route in the final checkpoint. If the harness cannot select worker models, complete
    the batch with the current model and state that no model switch occurred.

## Quality boundary

- Do not lower the evidence, applicability, locator, or limitation standards to save model cost.
- Escalate ambiguous citations, conflicting metadata, unclear methods, unsupported claims, or difficult
  applicability judgments to Sol even if they first appear during an operational stage.
- Use `xhigh` only for a specific difficult review that fails at `high`; do not make it the batch default.
- Preserve the user's explicit model choice when they name one for a particular task.

For non-Codex harnesses, map the same roles to that harness's balanced worker tier and flagship reasoning tier only
when explicit model routing is available. Never invent provider model IDs or claim that a switch occurred when the
harness cannot verify it.

I need to correct myself: **you don't need the Codex login.** You already have a direct line to Codex, and I found your Sonnet problem.

**What I checked:** ran `codex exec` three times against all three model tiers, confirmed the auth mode, read the plugin's agent file, confirmed my commit touched only one file.

## Found your Sonnet middleman

`~/.claude/plugins/cache/openai-codex/codex/1.0.6/agents/codex-rescue.md`

Line 4 says: `model: sonnet`

That's the `codex:rescue` subagent. Its own text calls it a "thin forwarding wrapper" — it's supposed to just pass work to Codex. But it's still a model that gets to *decide* whether to forward. Sometimes it doesn't. That's your "it really wasn't hitting Codex."

## You already have the direct path

I tested it. All three work right now, no proxy, no middleman:

```
codex exec --model gpt-5.6-sol   "..."
codex exec --model gpt-5.6-terra "..."
codex exec --model gpt-5.6-luna  "..."
```

Codex CLI 0.147.0, logged in on your ChatGPT subscription, already defaulted to `gpt-5.6-sol` at high effort.

**So skip the wrapper.** Use `codex exec` when you want Codex.

## I was wrong earlier

My first note said Claude Code had no way to reach those models, so Model Router was the missing piece. Not true. I've corrected the file.

## What I did about it

Your `sports-science-research-grounding` skill had that Terra/Sol routing plan that always gave up. I gave it the real commands and made it *try* before claiming it can't switch.

Committed and pushed to branch `worktree-codex-direct-routing`. To make it live:

```
cd ~/.claude/skills && git merge worktree-codex-direct-routing
```

## Don't log in to Codex on the proxy

It buys you nothing you don't have, and burns the same ChatGPT quota down a longer road.

**Your call, two options:**

1. **Leave the proxy installed and idle** *(what I'd do)*. Costs nothing. It's there if you want `/fabsol` later.
2. **Log in to a different provider** — Gemini, Grok, or Kimi — but only if you actually pay for one of those. That's the only thing the proxy gives you that Codex doesn't.

## One unrelated thing

Every Codex run printed this:

> Exceeded skills context budget. All skill descriptions were removed and 187 additional skills were not included

Codex can't see any of your skills right now. Separate problem, not from anything today. Say the word and I'll look.

# Codex "Exceeded skills context budget" — diagnosis (2026-08-15)

## The warning

Every `codex exec` run prints:

> Exceeded skills context budget. All skill descriptions were removed and 187
> additional skills were not included in the model-visible skills list.

## What it means

Codex has too many skills installed. It degrades in two stages:

1. Drops every skill **description** (so it can't tell what a skill is for).
2. Still can't fit, so it drops 187 skills from the list entirely.

Net effect: **Codex is blind to almost all your skills.** It will not auto-trigger
them, because it cannot see what they do.

## What I found

There are **215 `SKILL.md` files** under `~/.codex`. 195 of those are in
`~/.codex/plugins/cache/`. You have 34 plugins enabled.

Biggest contributors:

| Skills | Plugin |
|---:|---|
| 35 | `mattpocock-skills@mattpocock` |
| 22 | `anthropic-skills@claude-cowork` |
| 14 | `superpowers@claude-plugins-official` |
| 10 | `context-mode@context-mode` |
| 10 | `firecrawl@claude-cowork` |
| 9 | `legal@claude-cowork` |
| 8 | `finance@claude-cowork` |
| 6 | `slack@openai-curated` |
| 5 | `google-calendar@openai-curated` |

## The important part: `enabled = false` does NOT fix this

Tested directly. Disabled four plugins worth **79 skills** using
`-c plugins."name".enabled=false`. The warning still said **exactly 187**.
Not one unit of movement.

Codex counts every `SKILL.md` **on disk** in the plugin cache, whether the plugin
is enabled or not. So editing `enabled` flags in `config.toml` is wasted effort.

Also confirmed: `codex plugin` has **no `disable` subcommand**. Only:

```
codex plugin add / list / marketplace / remove
```

`remove` is the one that deletes the cache directory. That is the only lever that works.

## Also tested (did not work)

- `-c features.skill_search=true` — no change. Still 187.

## Proof it is pure volume

Ran Codex against an empty `CODEX_HOME`. The warning changed to the mild version:

> Skill descriptions were shortened to fit the skills context budget. Codex can
> still see every skill, but some descriptions are shorter. Disable unused skills
> or plugins to leave more room for the rest.

Few skills → everything visible. Many skills → hard failure. Nothing is broken;
there is just too much installed.

## The fix

Remove plugins you do not use **inside Codex**. This deletes the cache, which is
what actually counts:

```
codex plugin remove mattpocock-skills@mattpocock
codex plugin remove anthropic-skills@claude-cowork
codex plugin remove legal@claude-cowork
codex plugin remove finance@claude-cowork
codex plugin remove firecrawl@claude-cowork
```

That is 84 skills removed. Reversible — `codex plugin add <name>` puts any of them back.

Removing a plugin from **Codex** does not touch your **Claude Code** skills. They
are separate installs in separate directories.

## How much does this matter?

**Low, for how you actually use Codex.** The `codex exec --model <id> "<spec>"`
routing works fine — you hand Codex a complete spec, so it does not need to
discover a skill on its own.

It matters if you use Codex **interactively** and expect it to reach for a skill
by itself. Right now it cannot.

# Codex skills budget — diagnosis and cross-harness plan (2026-08-15)

## Correction to my earlier advice

I first recommended removing five plugins to free up space. **Do not run that list.**
`anthropic-skills@claude-cowork` carries your own skills — `five-slides-generator`,
`humanizer`, `session-handoff`, `morning`, `consolidate-memory`. Removing it would
have deleted the cross-harness portability you built on purpose.

## The warning

```
Exceeded skills context budget. All skill descriptions were removed and
187 additional skills were not included in the model-visible skills list.
```

Codex has too many skills. It degrades in two stages: first it drops every skill
**description**, then it drops 187 skills from the list entirely.

## The real problem — your portability is already broken

You keep skills in both harnesses so a project started in Claude Code just works
in Codex. Measured today, that is not happening:

- **150** personal skills in `~/.claude/skills/`
- **30** share a name with something Codex can reach — and that is an *upper bound*.
  Several are name collisions (`code-review`, `research`, `triage`, `handoff`,
  `teach`, `implement` are generic names owned by other plugins), so true overlap
  is lower.
- **120** are not in Codex in any form.

Missing from Codex are exactly the project-critical ones:

`sports-science-research-grounding`, `meeting-sync`, `graphify`, `status-report`,
`project-triage`, `closeout`, `weekly-review`, `interview-me`, `ingest-resource`,
`memory-write`, `fireflies-intake`, `pp-catapult-openfield-connect`, `pp-fireflies`,
`pp-zotero-research-library`, `CreateSkill`, `LifeOS`, `Harvest`, `meeting-prep`.

And even the skills that *are* reachable, Codex cannot see — descriptions were
dropped. So it will not auto-trigger any of them.

**The budget is being spent on third-party bundles you do not need in both places,
while your own skills are not there at all.** That is backwards.

## Mechanism confirmed: symlinks work

Tested. Symlinked one skill:

```bash
ln -s ~/.claude/skills/graphify ~/.codex/skills/graphify
```

The warning went from **187** to **188**. Codex follows symlinks into
`~/.codex/skills/` and counts them.

This gives one source of truth: the skill lives in your `claude-skills` git repo,
and both harnesses read the same files. Edit once, both are current. No copying,
no drift. (Probe symlink has been removed; nothing is changed yet.)

## What does NOT work

- `enabled = false` in `config.toml` — tested. Disabled four plugins worth **79
  skills**; the count stayed at exactly 187. Codex counts every `SKILL.md` on disk
  in the plugin cache, enabled or not.
- `-c features.skill_search=true` — no change.
- There is no `codex plugin disable`, and no `codex skills` subcommand. Only
  `codex plugin remove`, which deletes the cache directory. That is the only lever.

## Plan — remove first, then add

Order matters. Adding skills into a home that is already overflowing means the new
ones land in the same overflow and you cannot tell if they worked.

**Phase 1 — free up room.** Remove third-party bundles that do not need to exist
in both harnesses:

```bash
codex plugin remove mattpocock-skills@mattpocock   # 35 skills
codex plugin remove legal@claude-cowork            #  9
codex plugin remove finance@claude-cowork          #  8
codex plugin remove firecrawl@claude-cowork        # 10
```

62 skills freed. All reversible with `codex plugin add`.
**Keep** `anthropic-skills@claude-cowork` — that one is yours.

**Phase 2 — read the meter.** Re-run any `codex exec` and read the warning text:

| Warning says | Meaning |
|---|---|
| "…additional skills were not included" | still over budget, remove more |
| "descriptions were shortened… can still see every skill" | good regime, room to add |

**Phase 3 — link your own skills in.** One symlink per skill you actually want
portable. Start with the project-critical set, not all 120.

## How much this matters

Low for `codex exec --model <id> "<spec>"` routing — you hand Codex a full spec,
so it does not need to discover a skill.

High for what you actually described: picking up a project in Codex and having it
just work. That depends on Codex seeing the skill, which today it cannot.

# Codex "Exceeded skills context budget" — diagnosis (2026-08-15)

## The warning

Every `codex exec` run prints:

> Exceeded skills context budget. All skill descriptions were removed and 187
> additional skills were not included in the model-visible skills list.

## What it means

Codex has too many skills installed. It degrades in two stages:

1. Drops every skill **description** (so it can't tell what a skill is for).
2. Still can't fit, so it drops 187 skills from the list entirely.

Net effect: **Codex is blind to almost all your skills.** It will not auto-trigger
them, because it cannot see what they do.

## What I found

There are **215 `SKILL.md` files** under `~/.codex`. 195 of those are in
`~/.codex/plugins/cache/`. You have 34 plugins enabled.

Biggest contributors:

| Skills | Plugin |
|---:|---|
| 35 | `mattpocock-skills@mattpocock` |
| 22 | `anthropic-skills@claude-cowork` |
| 14 | `superpowers@claude-plugins-official` |
| 10 | `context-mode@context-mode` |
| 10 | `firecrawl@claude-cowork` |
| 9 | `legal@claude-cowork` |
| 8 | `finance@claude-cowork` |
| 6 | `slack@openai-curated` |
| 5 | `google-calendar@openai-curated` |

## The important part: `enabled = false` does NOT fix this

Tested directly. Disabled four plugins worth **79 skills** using
`-c plugins."name".enabled=false`. The warning still said **exactly 187**.
Not one unit of movement.

Codex counts every `SKILL.md` **on disk** in the plugin cache, whether the plugin
is enabled or not. So editing `enabled` flags in `config.toml` is wasted effort.

Also confirmed: `codex plugin` has **no `disable` subcommand**. Only:

```
codex plugin add / list / marketplace / remove
```

`remove` is the one that deletes the cache directory. That is the only lever that works.

## Also tested (did not work)

- `-c features.skill_search=true` — no change. Still 187.

## Proof it is pure volume

Ran Codex against an empty `CODEX_HOME`. The warning changed to the mild version:

> Skill descriptions were shortened to fit the skills context budget. Codex can
> still see every skill, but some descriptions are shorter. Disable unused skills
> or plugins to leave more room for the rest.

Few skills → everything visible. Many skills → hard failure. Nothing is broken;
there is just too much installed.

## The fix

Remove plugins you do not use **inside Codex**. This deletes the cache, which is
what actually counts:

```
codex plugin remove mattpocock-skills@mattpocock
codex plugin remove anthropic-skills@claude-cowork
codex plugin remove legal@claude-cowork
codex plugin remove finance@claude-cowork
codex plugin remove firecrawl@claude-cowork
```

That is 84 skills removed. Reversible — `codex plugin add <name>` puts any of them back.

Removing a plugin from **Codex** does not touch your **Claude Code** skills. They
are separate installs in separate directories.

## How much does this matter?

**Low, for how you actually use Codex.** The `codex exec --model <id> "<spec>"`
routing works fine — you hand Codex a complete spec, so it does not need to
discover a skill on its own.

It matters if you use Codex **interactively** and expect it to reach for a skill
by itself. Right now it cannot.

# Codex skills budget — findings and what to do (2026-08-15)

## Why this matters to you

You bounce between Claude Code and Codex and keep skills in both so a project
picks up cleanly. This file is about why that is not working and what will fix it.

## What was actually done today

Removed (these stuck):

```
legal@claude-cowork        9 skills
finance@claude-cowork      8 skills
firecrawl@claude-cowork   10 skills
```

**Kept `mattpocock-skills`** — you use it in both harnesses.
**Kept `anthropic-skills@claude-cowork`** — it carries your own skills
(`five-slides-generator`, `humanizer`, `session-handoff`, `morning`,
`consolidate-memory`). An earlier draft of this file told you to remove it. That
was wrong; ignore it.

Result: the warning went from **187 excluded → 152 excluded**. Real improvement,
still over budget.

## The wall: a 47-skill floor you cannot remove

`openai-curated-remote` (openai-templates, superpowers, google-drive, github,
gmail, heygen, fireflies, plugin-management) is a **built-in remote catalog**.

- It does not appear in `codex plugin marketplace list`
- `codex plugin marketplace remove openai-curated-remote` → *"not configured or installed"*
- I removed all 7 of its plugins. Codex re-downloaded all 47 skills within minutes.

Those 47 skills are permanent. They consume **13,605 characters** of description
budget before any of your own skills are considered.

## The budget is tokens, not skill count

This is the part that changes the strategy.

| Set | Skills | Description chars |
|---|---:|---:|
| Immovable remote floor | 47 | 13,605 |
| A 25-skill personal set | 25 | 11,503 |

Your skills average **460 characters** of description each. The floor averages **289**.
Yours are ~60% more expensive per skill.

Tested a clean home containing *only* 25 of your personal skills plus the
unavoidable floor: **still 16 skills excluded.**

So the usable budget is roughly **20,000 characters** of description total. The
floor already eats two-thirds of it. That leaves room for roughly **20–25 of your
own skills** — not 150.

## What does not work

- `enabled = false` in `config.toml` — disabled 79 skills' worth, count did not
  move one unit. Codex counts every `SKILL.md` on disk, enabled or not.
- `-c features.skill_search=true` — no change.
- No `codex plugin disable`. No `codex skills` subcommand. Only
  `codex plugin remove`, and it does not hold against the remote catalog.

## What does work: symlinks

Confirmed. Symlinking a Claude Code skill into `~/.codex/skills/` registers it —
the count moved 187 → 188.

```bash
ln -s ~/.claude/skills/<name> ~/.codex/skills/<name>
```

One source of truth. The skill stays in your `claude-skills` git repo; both
harnesses read the same file. Edit once, both current, no drift, nothing to sync.

## The strategy this points to

**Curate, do not mirror.** Pick the ~20 skills you actually reach for when picking

# Codex skills budget — diagnosis and cross-harness plan (2026-08-15)

## Correction to my earlier advice

I first recommended removing five plugins to free up space. **Do not run that list.**
`anthropic-skills@claude-cowork` carries your own skills — `five-slides-generator`,
`humanizer`, `session-handoff`, `morning`, `consolidate-memory`. Removing it would
have deleted the cross-harness portability you built on purpose.

## The warning

```
Exceeded skills context budget. All skill descriptions were removed and
187 additional skills were not included in the model-visible skills list.
```

Codex has too many skills. It degrades in two stages: first it drops every skill
**description**, then it drops 187 skills from the list entirely.

## The real problem — your portability is already broken

You keep skills in both harnesses so a project started in Claude Code just works
in Codex. Measured today, that is not happening:

- **150** personal skills in `~/.claude/skills/`
- **30** share a name with something Codex can reach — and that is an *upper bound*.
  Several are name collisions (`code-review`, `research`, `triage`, `handoff`,
  `teach`, `implement` are generic names owned by other plugins), so true overlap
  is lower.
- **120** are not in Codex in any form.

Missing from Codex are exactly the project-critical ones:

`sports-science-research-grounding`, `meeting-sync`, `graphify`, `status-report`,
`project-triage`, `closeout`, `weekly-review`, `interview-me`, `ingest-resource`,
`memory-write`, `fireflies-intake`, `pp-catapult-openfield-connect`, `pp-fireflies`,
`pp-zotero-research-library`, `CreateSkill`, `LifeOS`, `Harvest`, `meeting-prep`.

And even the skills that *are* reachable, Codex cannot see — descriptions were
dropped. So it will not auto-trigger any of them.

**The budget is being spent on third-party bundles you do not need in both places,
while your own skills are not there at all.** That is backwards.

## Mechanism confirmed: symlinks work

Tested. Symlinked one skill:

```bash
ln -s ~/.claude/skills/graphify ~/.codex/skills/graphify
```

The warning went from **187** to **188**. Codex follows symlinks into
`~/.codex/skills/` and counts them.

This gives one source of truth: the skill lives in your `claude-skills` git repo,
and both harnesses read the same files. Edit once, both are current. No copying,
no drift. (Probe symlink has been removed; nothing is changed yet.)

## What does NOT work

- `enabled = false` in `config.toml` — tested. Disabled four plugins worth **79
  skills**; the count stayed at exactly 187. Codex counts every `SKILL.md` on disk
  in the plugin cache, enabled or not.
- `-c features.skill_search=true` — no change.
- There is no `codex plugin disable`, and no `codex skills` subcommand. Only
  `codex plugin remove`, which deletes the cache directory. That is the only lever.

## Plan — remove first, then add

Order matters. Adding skills into a home that is already overflowing means the new
ones land in the same overflow and you cannot tell if they worked.

**Phase 1 — free up room.** Remove third-party bundles that do not need to exist
in both harnesses:

```bash
codex plugin remove mattpocock-skills@mattpocock   # 35 skills
codex plugin remove legal@claude-cowork            #  9
codex plugin remove finance@claude-cowork          #  8
codex plugin remove firecrawl@claude-cowork        # 10
```

62 skills freed. All reversible with `codex plugin add`.
**Keep** `anthropic-skills@claude-cowork` — that one is yours.

**Phase 2 — read the meter.** Re-run any `codex exec` and read the warning text:

| Warning says | Meaning |
|---|---|
| "…additional skills were not included" | still over budget, remove more |
| "descriptions were shortened… can still see every skill" | good regime, room to add |

**Phase 3 — link your own skills in.** One symlink per skill you actually want
portable. Start with the project-critical set, not all 120.

## How much this matters

Low for `codex exec --model <id> "<spec>"` routing — you hand Codex a full spec,
so it does not need to discover a skill.

High for what you actually described: picking up a project in Codex and having it
just work. That depends on Codex seeing the skill, which today it cannot.

You bounce between Claude Code and Codex and keep skills in both so a project
picks up cleanly. This file is about why that is not working and what will fix it.

budget before any of your own skills are considered.

## The budget is tokens, not skill count

This is the part that changes the strategy.

| Set | Skills | Description chars |
|---|---:|---:|

unavoidable floor: **still 16 skills excluded.**

floor already eats two-thirds of it. That leaves room for roughly **20–25 of your
own skills** — not 150.

up a project in Codex, and symlink those. Trying to make all 150 portable will not
fit and will keep Codex blind to all of them.

1. **Pick ~20 skills.** Biggest and simplest win.

   nearly double how many fit. `CreateSkill` alone is 1,008 characters.

(`anthropic-skills`), used in both (`mattpocock-skills`), or immovable (the floor).

work. That needs Codex to see the skill, and today it cannot.

# Meeting Sync

Pull new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault. Each meeting becomes one markdown file at `Inbox/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD_<title>.md`.

## Paths — shared config

Vault and state-file paths live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.json` (single source of truth):
- `vault_inbox_meetings` — export target (`/Users/kristinarash/SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings`)
- `meeting_sync_state_file` — idempotency ledger (`.sync-state.json` in that folder)
- `meeting_lookback_days` — default window (14)

`scripts/sync.py` reads these itself; don't hardcode paths elsewhere. If the vault ever moves, edit the config only.

sync.py passes `--limit 100000` to `transcripts find` — the CLI's default is 100, which silently truncates large backfills. Don't remove that flag.

## Prerequisite — one-time auth

Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` environment variable (see the `pp-fireflies` skill's Auth Setup). Verify with `fireflies-pp-cli doctor --agent` — the JSON must show `"auth": "configured"`. `scripts/sync.py` runs this check itself and exits with code 4 if auth is missing. In that case, stop and tell the user:

> Fireflies isn't authenticated yet. Set `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` in your environment (System Properties → Environment Variables on Windows), then restart your terminal. After that, `/meeting-sync` will work.

Do not try to fix auth yourself (no `auth set-token` — the env var is the canonical mechanism). Then exit.

## Sync flow

### 1. Run the pipeline script

The deterministic pipeline (doctor check → CLI sync → find → state diff → export → state update) is fully implemented in `scripts/sync.py`. Two-phase invocation:

**Phase A — list pending, check titles:**
```bash
python scripts/sync.py --list-only [--days-back N]
```
Prints a JSON array of not-yet-exported transcripts: `[{"id", "title", "date"}]`. Diagnostics go to stderr.

**Phase B — export:**
```bash
python scripts/sync.py --no-sync [--days-back N]
```
Prints a JSON array of newly exported absolute file paths (`--no-sync` skips the redundant DB refresh Phase A just did). Exports are detected by diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export — never "most recent .md" — so a no-op export can't claim an unrelated file.

`[days-back]` argument from the user maps to `--days-back N`; otherwise the config default applies.

### 2. Between phases: generic-title judgment (model's job)

The user does not name their Fireflies meetings consistently. Generic titles produce useless filenames in the vault. Check each pending `title` from Phase A against the generic patterns documented in the `name-meetings` skill (empty, `Zoom Meeting`, `Recording`, `Meeting`, date-only, etc.).

- **0 generics:** run Phase B immediately, silently.
- **1–3 generics:** use `AskUserQuestion` once — question: "N of the new meetings have generic titles. Name them before exporting?" with options **[Propose names first / Export as-is]**. If "Propose names first", invoke the `name-meetings` skill scoped to just these IDs, then re-run Phase A to pick up renamed titles before Phase B.
- **4+ generics:** report the count and suggest: *"Several new meetings have generic titles. Run `/name-meetings` to clean them up — I'll proceed with the export either way."* Then run Phase B without blocking.

This keeps the rename loop tight at sync-time without blocking the pipeline.

### 3. Augment each exported file (model's job)

For each path in Phase B's JSON output, the file is raw Fireflies markdown. Insert the fixed 5-section header from `assets/meeting-header.md` (this skill's folder) at the top — after frontmatter, before any existing content. Read the asset and prepend it verbatim.

Leave the Fireflies-generated transcript and summary below this block intact. This gives the user **5 fixed sections to fill in or curate** during interview-me / weekly-review, on top of the raw Fireflies content.

## Drift audit (periodic, not every sync)

A vault filename is a snapshot of the Fireflies title at export time. Titles get renamed afterwards, so the two drift apart. `scripts/audit_filenames.py` detects this by asking the export CLI to regenerate every filename into a scratch dir and diffing against the ledger — **the slug algorithm is never reimplemented**, the CLI is the authority.

```bash
python scripts/audit_filenames.py [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--skip-linkcheck] [--report PATH]
```

Run it from `weekly-review`, or on demand — **not** on every sync (it spawns one CLI call per ledger entry, ~2-4 min for a full vault). Same exit codes as sync.py; drift itself is not an error, read the counts in the JSON.

It classifies every mismatch, and the classes need different responses:

- **`regression`** — the vault name is good and Fireflies has reverted to an auto-generated stamp (`Jan_19_0445_PM`, `Untitled`, `Audio_Message`). **Never re-export these — it destroys the good name.** Fix the title upstream in Fireflies instead. Note the API refuses title updates on some older meetings; if so, say so and leave the vault alone (the ledger already protects it).
- **`semantic`** — the title genuinely differs in meaning. Usually two generations of AI naming rather than rot, so it needs a human call, not an automatic rename. Surface it, don't act.
- **`cosmetic`** — same words, different separators (`RTP_UpperExtremity` vs `RTP___Upper_Extremity`). Ignore; re-exporting is pure churn.

Before proposing any rename, check `inbound_links` in the output. Renaming a vault file breaks `[[wikilinks]]` from weekly-review notes and `GRAPH_REPORT.md`. Rewrite those links in the same pass or leave the file alone.

## Output to user

When done, report:
- N transcripts found in the window (stderr line from sync.py)
- M new exports written
- Path: `Inbox/meetings/`
- If 0 new: just say "No new meetings since last sync."

Keep it to 3 lines.

## Error handling

sync.py exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/config, 3 sync/find failure, 4 auth not configured.

- **Exit 4 (auth):** deliver the auth message from Prerequisite above, stop.
- **Exit 3 (sync/find):** report the stderr error verbatim, do not try to recover. The user may need to refresh their API key.
- **Export fails for one transcript:** sync.py logs a warning to stderr and continues with the rest; relay which one failed.
- **State file corrupted:** sync.py backs it up to `.sync-state.json.bak` and recreates fresh automatically (re-export is idempotent on the filesystem because filenames are deterministic per CLI); flag this in the report if the warning appears.

## What NOT to do

- **Don't re-implement steps the script owns** — doctor, CLI sync, find, state diff, export, state update all live in `scripts/sync.py`.
- **Don't identify exports by "newest .md file"** — that's the exact bug the directory-diff in sync.py fixes.
- **Don't detect filename drift by pattern-matching for "generic-looking" names** — that both misses real drift and invents fake drift. Use `audit_filenames.py`, which compares against what the export CLI actually produces.
- **Don't bulk re-export to "clean up" filenames.** Most mismatches are cosmetic or a second valid naming generation, and the `regression` class gets actively worse. Re-export only what a human approved.
- **Don't modify the Fireflies-generated content** of the exported file — only PREPEND the header from `assets/meeting-header.md`. The transcript and AI summary stay untouched.
- **Don't sync every interaction.** Run sync only when explicitly invoked OR when called by weekly-review / fireflies-intake.

# 5 Slides in 5 Minutes Generator

Generates polished, on-brand PowerPoint decks for Baylor Athletics' Applied Performance "5 Slides in 5 Minutes" Performance School education series. Each deck is a 5-minute cross-functional staff presentation that surfaces one topic, delivers a key insight, and sparks deeper conversation.

**Read [`references/code-template.md`](references/code-template.md) before writing any pptxgenjs code.** It contains the full structural template, design system constants, and common pitfalls.

**Read [`references/topic-library.md`](references/topic-library.md)** to understand the 40-topic library context when a topic is named.

**Read [`references/talking-points.md`](references/talking-points.md)** when generating speaker notes or when the user asks for a presenter version. Covers per-slide timing budget (~4:45 total) and talking-point structure.

**Read [`references/marp-template.md`](references/marp-template.md)** when the user asks for a "Marp version", "markdown slides", ".md version of the deck", or any version-controllable / shareable format alongside the pptx. Generates a second `.md` output mirroring the pptx narrative.

---

## The 5-Slide Narrative Structure

Every deck follows this fixed 5-slide arc, always in this order:

| Slide | Name | Purpose | Background |
|-------|------|---------|------------|
| 1 | Hook | Grab attention, frame the question | DARK |
| 2 | Problem / Context | Show the gap, the stakes, or the misunderstanding | LIGHT |
| 3 | Insight | The core scientific or practical concept | DARK |
| 4 | Application | What this looks like in practice for this audience | LIGHT |
| 5 | Takeaway | One clear point + a discussion question | DARK |

Dark/light alternation is a visual signature of the series. Never break this pattern.

---

## Full Workflow

### Step 1: Confirm the Topic

If the user gave a topic, proceed. If ambiguous, ask one clarifying question: "What's the core question you want answered in 5 minutes?"

### Step 2: Research the Content

Use WebSearch (or the firecrawl-search skill for full-page content) to gather 4-6 factual data points, statistics, or key findings on the topic. Prioritize:
- Peer-reviewed research findings
- Clinical or applied sport science data
- Practical frameworks used by elite programs

Take note of actual numbers and sources. Every stat in the deck must come from research, not fabrication.

### Step 3: Plan the Narrative

Before writing any code, draft the 5-slide narrative outline in the chat:

```
Slide 1 Hook:    [Provocative question or surprising stat]
Slide 2 Context: [The gap, problem, or misconception]
Slide 3 Insight: [The mechanism or framework]
Slide 4 Apply:   [Concrete example for the H&W team]
Slide 5 Take:    [One clear takeaway + discussion question]
```

### Step 4: Select the Color Palette

Choose a topic-appropriate 3-color palette. Never default to generic blue.

| Domain | Palette Ideas |
|--------|--------------|
| Sport Science / Technology | Navy + Cyan, Charcoal + Electric Teal |
| S&C / Power / Speed | Dark Charcoal + Orange/Amber, Forest + Gold |
| Recovery / Sleep | Deep Indigo + Soft Lavender, Dark Teal + Warm Amber |
| Mental Health / Psych | Deep Plum + Sage, Slate + Warm Rose |
| Nutrition / Fueling | Dark Forest + Fresh Green, Rich Brown + Gold |
| Load / Injury Risk | Dark Slate + Signal colors (green/yellow/red) |
| Athletic Medicine | Navy + Clinical White + Teal accent |

If the topic clearly maps to one domain row, pick that palette and proceed. If the mapping isn't obvious (topic spans domains, or the content may be institutional), ask with the **AskUserQuestion tool**: one question ("Which palette for this deck?"), offering the 2-3 most plausible domain palettes plus "Baylor brand" as options, each labeled with its colors. Put your best guess first with "(Recommended)" appended. The user can always pick Other and describe their own palette.

**Baylor brand colors** may be used as the palette when content is explicitly institutional:
- Baylor Green: `154734`
- Baylor Gold: `FFB81C`

Define three constants at the top of every script:
```javascript
const PRIMARY = "1B2A4A";   // Dark slide backgrounds + header bands
const ACCENT  = "00B4D8";   // Accent bars, highlights, key stats
const MUTED   = "94A3B8";   // Secondary text, subtitles
const WHITE   = "FFFFFF";
const LIGHT_BG = "F8FAFC";  // Light slide backgrounds
```

### Step 5: Build the Deck

Read `references/code-template.md` for the full working code template.

Install and run in a scratch build folder:
```powershell
$build = "$env:TEMP\five-slides"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $build | Out-Null
# write deck.js into $build, then:
Set-Location $build
npm install pptxgenjs 2>$null | Select-Object -Last 3
node deck.js    # writes deck.pptx into $build
```

**Required on every slide:**
- Series label: `"5 SLIDES · 5 MINUTES"` top-left, small tracked text, accent color
- Topic name: top-right, matching style
- Footer: `"Baylor Athletics · Applied Performance"` left, `"Slide N of 5"` right
- Left accent bar: 0.18" wide, full height, accent color (dark slides only)

### Step 6: QA

Export each slide to PNG via PowerPoint COM (PowerPoint is installed on this machine; close any open PowerPoint windows first):

```powershell
$build = "$env:TEMP\five-slides"
Remove-Item "$build\slide*.png" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$pp = New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application
$deck = $pp.Presentations.Open("$build\deck.pptx", $true, $false, $false)   # read-only, no window
foreach ($slide in $deck.Slides) { $slide.Export("$build\slide$($slide.SlideIndex).png", "PNG", 1500, 844) }
$deck.Close(); $pp.Quit()
Get-ChildItem "$build\slide*.png"
```

Read each slide PNG (the Read tool renders images). Check for: text overflow, overlapping elements, low-contrast text, missing content. Fix deck.js and re-verify once. If COM export fails (PowerPoint busy/locked), skip image QA and note that in the delivery message.

### Step 7: Deliver

Copy the finished deck out of the scratch folder and hand it to the user:
```powershell
Copy-Item "$env:TEMP\five-slides\deck.pptx" "$HOME\Desktop\[Topic]_5Slides5Minutes.pptx"
```

Send the file with the SendUserFile tool (or state the Desktop path plainly). Offer speaker notes as a follow-up if the user wants them.

### Step 8: Optional Marp markdown version

If the user asked for a "Marp version", "markdown slides", or ".md version of the deck", **also** generate a Marp-format markdown file using the pattern in `references/marp-template.md`. Reuse the exact same narrative, stats, and color palette — only the output format changes.

Write to `$HOME\Desktop\[Topic]_5Slides5Minutes.md`.

Tell the user: open the file in VS Code with the Marp extension, use the command palette → `Marp: Export slide deck` → pick HTML for a single shareable file viewable in any browser.

---

## Content Standards

- Every statistic is sourced from web search, never invented
- Cross-functional framing: each slide should give S&C, AT, Nutrition, Mental Health, and Sport Science a reason to care
- Tone: practitioner-to-practitioner — confident, direct, not academic
- "Surface level by design" — the deck opens a conversation, not closes one
- The discussion question on slide 5 is as important as the content

# Meeting Prep

Answers one question before the user walks into a room: **"Is everything I said I'd do actually reflected in the artifacts, and what do I need to raise?"**

The argument (or conversation context) names the project — e.g. FaceComps, RTP presentation, AppPerformance brief. If no project is named and none is obvious from context, ask which meeting this is for; that is the only question to ask.

## Step 1 — Reconstruct the "last agreed state"

Pull the most recent decisions about this project, cheapest source first:

1. Project memory files (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`) and global `MEMORY.md` active threads.
2. The most recent SecondBrain meeting note(s) mentioning the project (the meeting-sync output in the vault — **Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/_shared/config.json`, e.g. `vault_inbox_meetings`; load it if unsure — if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins).
3. If still thin, `memsearch search "<project> decision" --top-k 5`.

Produce a short internal list: what was decided, what was promised, by when.

## Step 2 — Verify the artifacts match

For each decided/promised item, check the actual artifact — not the conversation:

- Open the current deliverable files (deck, PDF, calendar, spreadsheet, app) and confirm the agreed change is present.
- `git log --since="<last meeting date>"` in the project repo to see what actually shipped.
- Note any artifact that is stale, locked, or missing.

Mark each item ✅ implemented / ⚠️ partially / ❌ not reflected.

## Step 3 — The brief

Output one screen, in this order:

```
## Meeting Prep — <project> (<meeting date/person if known>)

**Bottom line:** ready / ready with caveats / gaps found

**Since last meeting:** <2-4 bullets of what changed/shipped>

**Decision check:**
✅ <decision> — in <file path>
❌ <decision> — NOT reflected; <where it should be>

**Bring up in the meeting:** <open questions, items awaiting their input>

**Deliverables & paths:** <every file they might present or reference, full paths>
```

## Rules

- Verify against files, never against memory of the conversation — the whole point is catching drift between "we decided" and "it's in the deck."
- If a gap is small and mechanical (a label, a date), offer to fix it now in one line — don't just report it.
- Do not restructure or "improve" deliverables uninvited; this is a readiness check, not an editing pass.
- Brevity is the deliverable: the user is reading this minutes before a meeting.

# Project Triage

The user's daily project-portfolio dashboard. Renders an HTML view of every top-level folder in `~/Desktop/DEV/` with status pills (resume / pause / done / kill / archive), heuristic activity metrics, and curated purpose/action prose.

## Vault & files

- **Skill dir:** `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/project-triage/`
- **Script:** `triage.py` (Python 3.11+, no deps beyond stdlib)
- **Scan root:** `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/`
- **Output dir:** `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/`
- **Output file:** `YYYY-MM-DD.html` (one per day)
- **Curation file:** `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/.curation.json`
- **Python:** `python3` (from user's USER.md preference)

## Flow

### 1. Check whether today's already been generated

Glob `Desktop/DEV/project-triage/*.html`. If today's date file exists, ask:
> Today's triage already exists. Regenerate, or open the existing file?

If "open existing," just `start` it in the browser and exit.

### 2. Check for a missed yesterday

If today's file doesn't exist *and* yesterday's also doesn't exist, this is the morning-after case. Offer:
> Yesterday's triage was never generated. Want me to backfill it first, then run today's? (recommended)

If yes, run with `--date <yesterday>` first, then today's.

### 3. Generate the report

```bash
"C:/Python314/python.exe" "/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/project-triage/triage.py" --open
```

Pass `--date YYYY-MM-DD` for a backfill. The `--open` flag launches the default browser when generation succeeds.

### 4. Read the drift output

The script prints a `drift:` line listing projects whose curated state needs attention. Three drift signals:
- **Heuristic mismatch:** curated status disagrees with what the activity heuristics now say (e.g., curated "resume" but no files touched in 45d)
- **Stale curation:** the `curated_at` timestamp on the entry is > 30 days old
- **Active-but-uncurated:** a `resume`-classified project has no curated `purpose` (you haven't told the user what it does yet)

If `drift: 0`, the report stands on its own. Report:
> Today's triage at `Desktop/DEV/project-triage/<date>.html` · N projects · no drift.

If drift > 0, ALWAYS offer the curation pass — never silently update entries:
> N projects show drift. Want to walk through them now, or revisit later? (the ⚠ flags will stay in the dashboard until you do)

### 5. Curation pass (only if user opted in)

For each drifting project, use `AskUserQuestion` to surface ONE focused decision per project. Possible question shapes by drift type:

**Heuristic mismatch** (curated says X, heuristic says Y):
> `<project>` is curated as `<curated>` but heuristics now classify it as `<heuristic>`. What's the right call?
> - Keep curated status (override stays)
> - Adopt new heuristic status
> - New status: [other option]

**Stale curation** (>30d old, no heuristic disagreement):
> `<project>` was last curated `N` days ago. Quick re-confirmation:
> - Still accurate, refresh timestamp
> - Update purpose/action
> - Remove curation (let heuristics drive)

**Active-but-uncurated** (resume, no purpose):
> `<project>` is active but has no curated purpose. Want to add one?
> - Yes, I'll dictate purpose + action
> - Skip — leave heuristic-only
> - Mark for later (do nothing this run)

If the user wants to dictate prose, take their reply verbatim, update `.curation.json`, and stamp `curated_at` to now.

**Curation file schema:**
```json
{
  "<project-folder-name>": {
    "purpose": "string — what this project is and what it's for",
    "action": "string — next step or context for whether to touch it",
    "status_override": "resume|pause|done|kill|archive",
    "curated_at": "ISO-8601 datetime"
  }
}
```

Only the fields you're setting need to be present per entry. `status_override` is optional — when absent, heuristics drive the status.

After updates, re-run the script (without `--open`) so the saved HTML reflects the new curation:
```bash
"C:/Python314/python.exe" "/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/project-triage/triage.py"
```

### 6. Sign off

Three lines max:
- File: `Desktop/DEV/project-triage/<date>.html`
- Status counts: N resume, N pause, N done, N archive/kill
- Drift handled: N updated, N deferred (with the project names)

## What NOT to do

- **Don't auto-update `.curation.json` without explicit user approval per entry.** This file is sacred — it's the user's working judgment about their own work.
- **Don't run the script on directories outside `~/Desktop/DEV/`.** The whole point is that it's the DEV portfolio surface.
- **Don't generate prose for the user.** The user said heuristics-only + later evolves toward curation. When they're ready to add purpose/action, they tell you what to write. You don't infer it.
- **Don't reclassify a project as "kill" or "archive" without confirming.** Heuristic kill/archive in the dashboard is fine (it's just a recommendation), but if you're updating the curation file to override status, ask first.
- **Don't run more than once per day** unless the user explicitly asks to regenerate (e.g., after a curation pass, which is intentional).

## Edge cases

- **Backfill request for a date older than yesterday:** allow it (`--date YYYY-MM-DD`), but flag: *"Note: the script reads current file mtimes, not historical state. A backfill labels the report with that date but the metrics are from right now."*
- **Empty `DEV/`:** rare, but the script handles it cleanly (renders an empty dashboard). Tell the user there's nothing to triage.
- **Python missing or path differs:** fall back to `python3` then `python`. If all fail, surface the error verbatim and stop.

```bash
cd ~/.claude/skills && git merge worktree-codex-direct-routing
```

The symlinks point at the main checkout, so the trims take effect the moment you merge.

`anthropic-skills@claude-cowork` is a frozen snapshot. Its copies of your own skills

**The warning still says 171 excluded.** It did not move when I removed slack and

| Chars | Group |
|---:|---|
| 13,605 | **immovable** remote floor (`openai-curated-remote`, cannot be removed) |
| 6,370 | your 18 skills (after trim) |
| 6,126 | `mattpocock-skills` |
| **26,101** | **subtotal** — against a budget of roughly **20,000** |

That subtotal assumes **every other bundle is already gone**. It still does not fit.

## The one lever left

**Drop `mattpocock-skills` from Codex.** Floor (13,605) + your 18 skills (6,370) =
**19,975** — right at budget.

```bash
codex plugin remove mattpocock-skills@mattpocock
```

You said you use it in both harnesses, so I did not do this. It is your call, and it
is reversible with `codex plugin add`. You would keep it in Claude Code either way —
the two installs are separate.

If you would rather keep it, the honest position is: Codex will keep auto-triggering
poorly, and you drive it explicitly instead — which is what `codex exec` already does.

## Scope reminder

None of this affects `codex exec --model <id> "<spec>"` routing. That works. You hand
Codex a complete spec, so it never needs to discover a skill on its own.
